The method includes displaying a stream of images in a display area of a display device. During display of the image stream, a user’s point of regard on the display area is determined. Based on the determined point of regard, a first area within the display area is defined around that point.

A first part of an image that is shown within the first area is displayed using a first parameter value associated with an image characteristic. A second part of the same image, shown outside the first area, is displayed using a second parameter value for that same image characteristic. In this way, different regions of the displayed image may be presented with different visual properties depending on their relationship to the user’s point of regard.

The method further includes predicting the user’s point of regard for a future display time. This prediction is based on at least one result of an image-related analysis, such as analysis of image content, motion, object locations, scene changes, or other visual features within the image stream. The predicted point of regard may then be used to determine where the first area should be positioned for subsequently displayed images.
outputs.L4:
A method is provided for displaying a stream of images on a display device in a manner that takes into account where a user is expected to look. The method includes receiving or generating a sequence of images, such as video frames, graphical content, virtual reality imagery, augmented reality imagery, or other visual content intended to be presented to a user. For one or more images in the stream, image-related analysis is performed to estimate or predict a future point of regard of the user. The point of regard may correspond to a location within the displayed image, display surface, or viewing field at which the user is likely to direct visual attention at a later time.

The prediction may be based on one or more forms of analysis associated with the image stream. For example, the method may analyze motion within the images, object positions, object trajectories, scene changes, saliency information, contrast, brightness, edges, faces, text, or other visual features that are likely to attract user attention. In some implementations, the prediction may also use historical viewing behavior, gaze-tracking data, head-tracking data, user input, application state, or contextual information. Based on this analysis, the method determines a predicted future point of regard and defines a focal area around that point. The focal area may have any suitable shape, such as a circular, elliptical, rectangular, or irregular region, and may be sized according to confidence in the prediction, display characteristics, user preferences, available processing resources, or content type.

After the focal area has been determined, the image is displayed using different parameter values for image regions inside and outside the focal area. The portion of the image within the predicted focal area may be rendered, transmitted, processed, or displayed with a first set of parameters selected to provide higher visual quality. Regions outside the focal area may be rendered, transmitted, processed, or displayed with a second set of parameters selected to reduce computational load, bandwidth, memory use, power consumption, or other resource requirements. The parameters may include, for example, resolution, compression level, bit rate, frame rate, level of detail, sampling density, shading quality, color depth, filtering, sharpness, contrast, brightness, refresh rate, or other image-display or image-processing characteristics.

In one example, the predicted focal area is displayed at a higher resolution or with a lower compression ratio, while peripheral regions are displayed at a reduced resolution or with stronger compression. In another example, the focal area is rendered with greater detail, more accurate lighting, or higher sampling quality, while areas outside the focal area are rendered with simplified geometry, reduced texture quality, or fewer processing operations. A gradual transition region may be provided between the focal area and the surrounding area so that changes in parameter values are less noticeable to the user.

The predicted focal area may be updated continuously or periodically as the image stream changes. For each new image, group of images, or time interval, the method may repeat the analysis, update the predicted point of regard, redefine the focal area, and adjust the applicable display parameters. This allows the display process to adapt dynamically to moving objects, scene transitions, changes in user behavior, or changes in the visual content. If actual gaze data is available, the predicted point of regard may be compared with the user’s measured gaze position, and the prediction model may be corrected or refined over time.

By applying higher-quality or higher-resource processing primarily to the region where the user is expected to look, the method can maintain perceived image quality while reducing the amount of processing, transmission bandwidth, memory access, or electrical power required to display the image stream. Conversely, the method may also be used to allocate available resources preferentially to visually important regions, thereby improving perceived quality without increasing overall system load. The technique is applicable to a wide range of display systems, including televisions, monitors, mobile devices, head-mounted displays, gaming systems, remote rendering systems, video streaming platforms, and virtual or augmented reality environments.
outputs.L5:
A clear **Method** is essential for turning an idea into a practical and repeatable process. Whether in research, project management, or technical development, a method provides structure, defines steps, and helps ensure consistent results. Without a reliable method, decisions can become unclear and outcomes may be difficult to measure.

One useful concept in planning is **POR**, often understood as “Plan of Record.” A POR represents the agreed-upon plan that teams follow during execution. It may include goals, timelines, responsibilities, risks, and expected deliverables. By establishing a POR, organizations can align stakeholders and reduce confusion throughout a project.

The term **PORn** may appear as a variation, label, or internal shorthand depending on the context in which it is used. When working with specialized terminology, it is important to define terms clearly so that everyone involved understands their meaning. A strong method, combined with a well-documented POR and clear definitions for terms like PORn, can improve communication, planning, and overall project success.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an eye-tracking display method that predicts a viewer’s point of regard and renders the foveal region of an image stream with different image parameters than the peripheral region.
counterfactuals.output: A method for displaying image content using eye tracking includes receiving an image stream for presentation on a display, acquiring eye-position data of a viewer, and determining, from the eye-position data, a predicted point of regard on the display. A foveal region associated with the predicted point of regard is identified, and a peripheral region outside the foveal region is also identified. The method renders the foveal region using first image parameters and renders the peripheral region using second image parameters different from the first image parameters. The first and second image parameters may include one or more of resolution, refresh rate, bit depth, compression level, shading rate, color depth, contrast, luminance, or filtering. The rendered foveal and peripheral regions are combined for presentation as a display frame of the image stream. The predicted point of regard may be updated over successive frames to reduce perceived latency and maintain high-quality rendering in a viewer’s area of visual attention while reducing processing, bandwidth, or power consumption in peripheral areas.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate formal patent language describing foveated rendering for video playback, including reference numerals for the display device, user, point of regard, display area, first area, first image part, second image part, and prediction of the gaze point at a future display time.
counterfactuals.output:
In some embodiments, a display device **(100)** is configured to present video content to a user **(102)** by employing foveated rendering based on a point of regard of the user. The display device **(100)** may comprise a display area **(106)** configured to display a sequence of video images, an eye-tracking arrangement configured to determine or estimate a gaze direction of the user **(102)**, and one or more processors configured to render different portions of the video images at different image qualities based on a predicted gaze location.

More particularly, the one or more processors may be configured to determine a point of regard **(104)** of the user **(102)** relative to the display area **(106)**. The point of regard **(104)** may correspond to a location on, or associated with, the display area **(106)** at which the user **(102)** is looking. Based on the point of regard **(104)**, the processors may define a first area **(108)** of the display area **(106)**. The first area **(108)** may include, surround, or be otherwise associated with the point of regard **(104)**.

For a video image to be displayed, the processors may generate or obtain a first image part **(110)** corresponding to the first area **(108)** and a second image part **(112)** corresponding to at least one further area of the display area **(106)** outside the first area **(108)**. The first image part **(110)** may be rendered, decoded, filtered, upscaled, transmitted, or otherwise processed at a first quality level, and the second image part **(112)** may be rendered, decoded, filtered, upscaled, transmitted, or otherwise processed at a second quality level lower than the first quality level. The first quality level may comprise at least one of a higher spatial resolution, higher bit rate, higher sampling density, higher shading rate, lower compression level, higher frame quality, higher texture resolution, or higher reconstruction quality than the second quality level.

In certain embodiments, the display device **(100)** is configured to account for latency between gaze measurement and display of a corresponding video image. The one or more processors may receive gaze information indicative of a current or previously measured point of regard of the user **(102)** and generate a prediction **(114)** of the gaze point at a future display time. The future display time may correspond to a time at which a particular video frame, video field, or rendered image is expected to be presented on the display area **(106)**. The prediction **(114)** may be determined based on one or more of current gaze position, prior gaze positions, gaze velocity, gaze acceleration, head pose, head motion, content motion, saliency information, frame timing information, rendering latency, decoding latency, display refresh timing, or a motion model.

The first area **(108)** may be positioned relative to the predicted gaze point indicated by the prediction **(114)** rather than solely relative to a most recently measured gaze point. Accordingly, the first image part **(110)** may be arranged to coincide with or encompass the predicted point of regard at the future display time, thereby increasing perceived image quality in a region expected to be observed by the user **(102)** when the video image is displayed.

In one implementation, the first area **(108)** comprises a foveal region, and the second image part **(112)** comprises a peripheral region surrounding the first area **(108)**. The boundary between the first image part **(110)** and the second image part **(112)** may be fixed or variable, and may be selected based on gaze-tracking confidence, gaze velocity, display resolution, video content type, user-specific calibration data, or available processing or transmission resources. The display device **(100)** may further apply blending, interpolation, filtering, or gradual quality transitions between the first image part **(110)** and the second image part **(112)** to reduce perceptible artifacts.

In exemplary claim-style language, a method may comprise: determining, by a display device **(100)**, gaze information associated with a user **(102)**; determining, from the gaze information, a point of regard **(104)** with respect to a display area **(106)**; predicting, based at least in part on the gaze information, a predicted gaze point **(114)** at a future display time of a video image; defining a first area **(108)** of the display area **(106)** based on the predicted gaze point **(114)**; generating a first image part **(110)** corresponding to the first area **(108)** at a first quality level; generating a second image part **(112)** corresponding to a second area of the display area **(106)** outside the first area **(108)** at a second quality level lower than the first quality level; and displaying, by the display device **(100)**, the first image part **(110)** and the second image part **(112)** as at least part of the video image at the future display time.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention idea into a patent claim: use gaze tracking and image-related analysis to predict where the user will look in the next frame, then display that region of the frame with higher quality or different image characteristics than the rest of the screen.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A computer-implemented method** comprising:  
   receiving, by one or more processors, gaze data indicative of a current gaze location of a user viewing a display;  
   receiving image data corresponding to a current frame or one or more prior frames displayed on the display;  
   analyzing the gaze data and the image data to predict a future gaze region of the user in a subsequent frame to be displayed;  
   generating the subsequent frame such that the predicted future gaze region is rendered with a first image presentation characteristic and one or more regions outside the predicted future gaze region are rendered with a second image presentation characteristic different from the first image presentation characteristic; and  
   causing the subsequent frame to be displayed on the display,  
   wherein the first image presentation characteristic provides higher perceived visual quality than the second image presentation characteristic.

2. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the first image presentation characteristic comprises at least one of higher resolution, higher bitrate, reduced compression, higher contrast, higher brightness, higher color depth, higher refresh rate, reduced blur, or increased sharpening relative to the second image presentation characteristic.

3. **The method of claim 1**, wherein analyzing the image data comprises identifying at least one image feature selected from the group consisting of an object, a face, text, motion, saliency, scene context, edge density, depth information, or semantic content.

4. **The method of claim 1**, wherein predicting the future gaze region comprises applying a machine learning model to the gaze data and the image data.

5. **The method of claim 1**, wherein predicting the future gaze region is further based on a temporal history of gaze locations of the user.

6. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the predicted future gaze region corresponds to a region of the subsequent frame expected to fall within a foveal or parafoveal viewing area of the user.

7. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the one or more regions outside the predicted future gaze region are rendered with reduced quality to reduce at least one of processing load, graphics rendering load, memory bandwidth, display power consumption, or network bandwidth.

8. **A system** comprising:  
   a gaze-tracking sensor configured to generate gaze data associated with a user;  
   a display;  
   one or more processors; and  
   one or more memories storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the system to perform the method of claim 1.

9. **A non-transitory computer-readable medium** storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform the method of claim 1.

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a patent abstract in the style of an automotive/VR display invention, about subsequently displaying images where the user’s future point of regard is predicted and a region around it is rendered according to a different parameter value than regions outside it.
counterfactuals.output: A display system and method are provided for presenting image content to a user of a vehicle-mounted, head-mounted, or virtual-reality display. The system obtains gaze-related data associated with a current point of regard of the user and predicts, based on the gaze-related data and optionally head-motion, vehicle-state, scene, or user-history data, a future point of regard for a subsequently displayed image frame. A rendering controller defines a region of the image frame surrounding the predicted future point of regard and renders the region using a first value of a rendering parameter, while rendering one or more regions outside the defined region using a second value of the rendering parameter different from the first value. The rendering parameter may include resolution, refresh rate, brightness, contrast, color depth, shading rate, compression level, latency compensation, or image-enhancement strength. The image frame is then displayed such that visual quality, computational load, or power consumption is selectively optimized in accordance with the predicted future viewing direction of the user.
